study.title: Acupuncture Modulates the Spontaneous Activity and Functional Connectivity of Calcarine in Patients With Chronic Stable Angina Pectoris
study.study_design: Randomized controlled trial with parallel groups; resting-state fMRI study with 2-week baseline phase and 2-week treatment phase
study.randomization: Patients assigned into two groups randomly using a random number table
study.population: Chronic stable angina pectoris (CSAP) patients and healthy subjects (HS) from nearby communities
study.inclusion_criteria: CSAP patients: (1) aged from 45 to 80 years old; (2) right-handedness; (3) met the diagnostic criteria; (4) graded as level 1 or 2 of angina based on the angina grading system of the Canadian Cardiovascular Society; (5) coronary artery stenosis ≥50% on coronary angiography; (6) the duration of disease was longer than 3 months; (7) the frequency of angina attacks was more than twice a week. Healthy subjects: (1) aged from 45 to 80 years old; (2) right-handedness; (3) had no CSAP or other physical or psychological diseases.
study.exclusion_criteria: CSAP patients: (1) had an acute coronary syndrome, malignant arrhythmia, or myocardial infarction within the last 3 months; (2) suffered from other severe psychiatric, neurological, cardiovascular, respiratory, or renal disorders; (3) had a diagnosis of diabetes or impaired glucose tolerance; (4) suffered from other chronic pain disorders or having a history of head trauma; (5) had any contraindication to MRI scanning, such as claustrophobia; (6) the Zung Self-Rating Anxiety Scale (SAS) or Self-Rating Depression Scale (SDS) ≥50; (7) participated in other clinical trials within 3 months; (8) received acupuncture treatment in the past 3 months. Healthy subjects: (1) had any contraindication to MRI scanning, such as claustrophobia; (2) participated in other clinical trials within 3 months; (3) received acupuncture treatment in the past 3 months.

extraction_notes.note: Supplementary Table 1 (baseline fALFF comparison CSAP vs HS) is referenced but not provided in the PDF. Peak coordinates and cluster sizes for bilateral calcarine, left middle occipital gyrus, right superior temporal gyrus, and right postcentral gyrus were not extractable.

Supplementary Table 2 (fALFF changes pre vs post treatment) is referenced but not provided. Peak coordinates and cluster sizes for all pre-post fALFF changes (brainstem, hippocampus, parahippocampus, calcarine/cuneus, orbitofrontal gyri) were not extractable.
Supplementary Table 3 (between-group differences of fALFF changes in Group A vs Group B) is referenced but not provided. These data were not extractable.
Supplementary Table 4 (within-group rsFC change in Group A and Group B) is referenced but not provided. Peak coordinates and cluster sizes for within-group rsFC changes were not extractable.

Supplementary Table 5 (between-group comparison of rsFC change Group A vs Group B) is referenced but not provided. Peak coordinates and cluster sizes for the between-group rsFC differences were not extractable.
Supplementary Figure 1 (acupoint locations) is referenced but not provided.
Supplementary Figure 2 (between-group fALFF differences in Group A vs Group B) is referenced but not provided.
No adverse events were reported or explicitly described in the paper. The adverse events section is absent.
Expectancy, credibility, blinding success, and guessed allocation were not measured or reported in this study.
Sensory/deqi responses were described as procedural goals (to achieve deqi) but were not formally measured, quantified, or compared between groups.

The paper reports n=37 CSAP patients enrolled and 65 HS; 7 CSAP patients quit at baseline (leaving 30), and 1 was excluded for motion (leaving 29). But neuroimaging baseline comparison used n=37 CSAP. The n for the baseline fALFF comparison is inferred as n=37 CSAP vs n=65 HS.

Figure 2 shows t-statistic range labels (1.985 to 4.619 for baseline comparison; -4.727 to 4.826 for pre-post treatment) but these are color bar ranges from the figure and not specific peak t-values for individual clusters.

The abstract states 'left hippocampus, left thalamus' as separate clusters but the results text describes them jointly as 'left hippocampus/thalamus'. Figure 4B shows them potentially as the same cluster. Extracted as separate rows following the abstract description.
No Talairach or MNI coordinates are provided in the main text for any of the reported brain regions. All coordinates are in Supplementary Tables not provided.
The coordinate space is stated as MNI in the methods (normalization into MNI space). This is used as the coordinate_space_reported_exact for all neural results.
Group B within-group rsFC analysis: the paper states 'no significant rsFC change was found in Group B after treatment' – this is a null result and no cluster data are available.

BOLD sequence details: slice number = 30, total volumes = 180, but total scan duration in minutes is not explicitly stated. Approximate duration = 180 × 2000ms TR = 360 seconds = 6 minutes, but this is not directly stated and has not been extracted.

The paper does not report whether any sham acupuncture or placebo condition was included. Group B uses acupoints on the meridian indirectly related to the Heart (LI5, LI6) as an active control comparator, not sham needling.
Table 1 note: CSAP n=37 but only 29 had post-treatment MRI. The demographics in Table 1 are for all 37 CSAP patients vs 65 HS. The within-group fALFF and clinical analyses used n=29 patients.
